editorial:
You meet Quinn, a young nurse who downloads a creepy app that predicts exactly when she will die. The countdown feels personal and scary, especially when a shadowy figure starts showing up around her. The movie mixes jump scares with a race against time, so you feel pulled into her panic as hours disappear and every choice matters. You also see how the app turns ordinary moments into tense countdowns.

The cast keeps things fun, especially the comic relief from a priest and a fellow patient, while the pacing rarely slows down. Some scares are predictable, and the logic gets silly, but it is easy to enjoy if you want a quick horror night with friends.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Quinn learns the curse can be broken if someone dies before their countdown. She gets Dr. Sullivan to download the app, and the demon kills him when his short timer ends. Quinn's countdown resets to decades, but the twist comes when her sister Jordan reveals she also downloaded the app with only minutes left. Quinn rushes to Jordan, and the demon appears again, leaving their safety uncertain.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quick horror nights with friends.
